sections.label: Budget debate and Committee of Supply
sections.summary: The Budget debate had 65 speakers and 569 cuts, with 4,290 minutes spent and unanimous support for Budget 2021.

sentences.speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: For many of the Nominated Members, the Budget debate was the occasion of their first speech in Parliament.

sentences.speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: There were 65 speakers over the three days of the Budget debate, the highest number in the past five years.

sentences.speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: The Committee of Supply saw 569 cuts filed, also the highest number of cuts in the past five years.

sentences.speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: With backbenchers having up to 20 minutes of speech time, 18 minutes of cuts and additional time for clarifications, we spent 4,290 minutes, or 71.5 hours debating this year’s Budget and Committee of Supply, culminating in the unanimous support of all Members for Budget 2021.

sentences.speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: In addition, we cleared 195 Parliamentary Questions, dealt with one Adjournment Motion and a Ministerial Statement on a matter of some importance.

sections.label: Conversations on Women's Development
sections.summary: Ideas were canvassed to support women's career, parenthood and care-giving aspirations, with a White Paper planned later this year.

sentences.speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: They canvassed ideas to support women in their career and parenthood aspirations, as well as their care-giving responsibilities.

sentences.speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: We will also be having the Conversations on Women's Development, with a view to a White Paper later this year, as mentioned by Minister of State Sun Xueling.

sections.label: Reserves draw and fiscal deficit
sections.summary: A draw on reserves of up to $53.7 billion was sought, with 50% of net investment income and returns already used.

sentences.speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: We began the financial year with a deficit following a year that saw the largest deficit in our history due to circumstances beyond our control.

sentences.speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: We have had to seek a draw on our reserves to the tune of up to $53.7 billion to fight the crisis.

sentences.speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: Current revenues and taxes are inevitably impacted by the economic downturn.

sentences.speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: We are already using 50% of our net investment income (NII) and net investment returns (NIR).

sections.label: GST raise timing
sections.summary: The GST raise remains on the cards, with exact timing subject to the economic outlook.

sentences.speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: As these structural trends remain unchanged, the GST raise remains on the cards with the exact timing subject to the economic outlook.

sections.label: GST increase support measures
sections.summary: DPM Heng cited fiscal prudence and three measures: enhanced GST vouchers, a $6 billion Assurance Package, and a fair tax system.

sentences.speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: Deputy Prime Minister Heng addressed these, explaining the need for fiscal prudence in order to ensure fiscal sustainability.

sentences.speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: He reiterated the Government's commitment to help our people manage the impact of the GST rate increase through: first, enhancement of the permanent GST voucher scheme when the GST rate is raised; second, the $6 billion Assurance Package to offset the GST increase which will effectively delay the GST rate increase for the majority of Singaporean households for five years and 10 years, for lower income Singaporeans; and third, keeping our overall taxes and transfer system fair and progressive.

sentences.speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: In a tight fiscal situation, this Parliament will not be able to avoid having to make difficult decisions.

sentences.speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: We will have to choose between what may be popular and what is right.

sections.label: 569 cuts highest in decade
sections.summary: The 569 cuts are the highest in the last decade, not only in five years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: I will not repeat the details that the Leader has shared but clearly, it has been a really long session.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: But the 569 cuts that Leader mentioned is not only the highest in five years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: Actually, it is the highest in the last decade!

sections.label: Women's Charter 60th anniversary
sections.summary: The speaker notes this year is the 60th anniversary of the Women's Charter, with moves begun in 1961.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: I think the ayes have it; the ayes have it!

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: We may not realise that this year is also the 60th anniversary of the Women's Charter in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: We began putting in place these moves many years ago in 1961.

sections.label: Leaders versus politicians question
sections.summary: The passage asks whether we are leaders or politicians.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: The question we need to ask ourselves: are we leaders or are we politicians?

sections.label: MSE and MCCY budget cuts
sections.summary: MSE received 80 cuts and MCCY 50, which the passage says tells us something.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: MSE receiving 80 cuts, with MCCY coming in second with 50, tell us something.

sections.label: Unanimous support for Budget
sections.summary: As in past years, there is unanimous support for the Budget and the Government's approach despite alternative views and disagreements on details.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: Like past years, there is a unanimous support for the Budget and the Government's approach even if there are alternative views and disagreements on some details.

sections.label: Foreign interest in Singapore's COVID response
sections.summary: Foreign politicians, officials, business leaders, medical experts and media were keen to understand Singapore's contact tracing, technology, hospital management, Budget programmes and financing.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: Many politicians, government officials, business leaders, medical experts and media there were very keen to understand what we were doing in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: They envied our contact tracing efforts and the use of technology to help with the SafeEntry and TraceTogether token.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: The way we managed our hospitals and healthcare resources without straining struck a chord with them as they were struggling.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: They were surprised at how extensive our Budget programmes were at every level to look after our people and to keep the economy going, and were even more surprised at how we financed it.

sections.label: Budgets 2020 and 2021 positioning
sections.summary: Budgets 2020 parts 1 to 5 and Budget 2021 will deal with the present and position Singapore for the future.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: Budgets 2020 parts 1 to 5, and Budget 2021 – I am not whether there are other further parts – will not only decisively deal with the here and now, but also position ourselves for the future.
